decisions.reason: A classic lever handle line sits squarely in the firm's core design and fitting know-how, so the firm can read early results and refine the models rather than withdraw them.
A lever handle family builds directly on established ergonomic and fixing-technology knowledge and fits the firm's push toward broad system families, making it cheap to sustain and improve.
A single handle design is closely related to existing competence, but as a one-off it carries somewhat more risk of being consolidated within a year.
Like C, it draws on core design know-how and is easy to assess, but a standalone design is more exposed to range pruning.
A handle family with several models fits the firm's knowledge base and its system-breadth strategy, so keeping it is the expected course.
The L700 electronic access system is the firm's flagship toward digital building organization, and in-house R&D and patented engineering give it the absorptive capacity to keep developing it.
